The three prints work beautifully as a trio. The left print shows a coastal café table laid with seafood, wine and olives, with sailboats drifting across a pale blue bay in the background. The right print returns to a sun-drenched terrace scene: a round café table set with a small feast of antipasti, fresh flowers and drinks, with the whitewashed hillside town and shimmering blue sea stretching out behind. The soft blue and white tones play really well with brushed chrome or matt white fixtures, and if you've got any natural wood shelving or rattan accessories in there, the warm terracotta and earthy tones in the prints will pick those up beautifully. For a full Mediterranean mood, pair with white fluffy towels, a terracotta pot or two, and maybe a trailing plant on a shelf.

Choosing the Right Size and Finish for Your Space

Before you pick a size, it's worth holding a piece of paper up to your wall (or using painter's tape) to mark out how much space you actually have. That said, if you have a generous wall above a freestanding bath, don't be shy about going bigger; the detail in these illustrations really rewards a closer look at a larger size.

aiItems.content:
What is decor for bathroom?

Bathroom decor refers to the decorative items you add to a bathroom to give it personality, warmth and style — and wall art prints are one of the most effective ways to do that. A well-chosen set of prints can make a plain bathroom feel like a considered, designed space rather than a purely functional room. In a coastal or Mediterranean style, soft blue and white tones with painted or illustrative artwork are especially popular, as they create a calm, airy feel that suits the relaxing nature of a bathroom. Choosing prints that are moisture-aware — such as canvas-wrapped options — means your decor stays looking great even in a steamy environment.

How to Hang Decor for Bathroom: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough clear space for all three prints side by side — above the bath, behind the loo or beside the sink are all great spots. Avoid walls directly above a shower where steam and splashes are most intense.

2. Decide on your layout: For a set of three, a straight horizontal row at eye level is the most timeless arrangement. Mark the centre point of your wall and work outward, leaving an equal gap (around 5–8 cm) between each print.

3. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is noticeable with three prints in a row. A small spirit level or a spirit-level app on your phone will save you a lot of re-hanging.

4. Pick the right hanging method: In a bathroom, damage-free adhesive picture strips work well on tiled or painted walls and avoid the need for drilling. For heavier framed options, a single picture hook into a wall stud is the most secure.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back to check the spacing and alignment before you commit. It's much easier to make small adjustments now than after everything is fully secured.

Which Option Is Right for Your Bathroom? Comparing Print Formats

Unframed Print (Luster or Museum paper) — The most affordable option; you choose your own frame. Best for well-ventilated bathrooms or other rooms. Luster paper gives a soft, semi-gloss finish; Museum quality paper delivers the richest, deepest colour reproduction.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum paper) — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no frame-hunting needed. A great choice if you want a polished, finished look immediately. Best suited to bathrooms with good ventilation rather than very high moisture.

Wrapped Canvas — The best choice for damp, steamy bathrooms. Canvas is moisture-resistant, making it far more durable in high-humidity environments than paper prints. Also arrives ready to hang, with the print wrapped neatly around a solid frame — no additional framing required. A beautiful, gallery-style finish.

aiItems.content:
What is a bathroom painting?

A bathroom painting is a piece of wall art — typically a print, canvas, or original artwork — chosen specifically to be displayed in a bathroom, restroom, or WC. Because bathrooms tend to be smaller, more functional spaces, bathroom paintings are a simple and affordable way to add personality, colour, and a decorative focal point without a full redecoration. Popular styles include coastal, botanical, abstract, and typographic designs, and they work in everything from compact cloakrooms to large family bathrooms. For damp or steamy bathrooms, a moisture-resistant option such as a wrapped canvas print is usually the most practical choice.

How to Hang a Bathroom Painting Set of 3

1. Measure your wall first: Use a tape measure to find the total width of the wall or the section you want to fill. Aim for the combined width of all three prints to cover around two-thirds of that space — this keeps things balanced and avoids the prints looking too small or too cramped.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall section and use a pencil to mark it lightly. Hang the middle print centred on this mark, then work outwards to position the left and right prints with an equal gap between each one — 5 to 8 cm is a good starting point.

3. Hang at eye level: The centre of each print should sit at roughly eye level, which for most people is around 145–150 cm from the floor. In a bathroom where you spend time seated (near a toilet or bath), you can go slightly lower so the art is comfortable to look at from that position.

4. Use a spirit level: Even small differences in height are very noticeable with a set of three. A small spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone takes seconds and saves a lot of frustration.

5. Consider moisture: In a steamy bathroom, choose the canvas-wrapped option for your prints — it's moisture-resistant and will last far longer than a paper print in a high-humidity environment.

Choosing Your Bathroom Painting Format: Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print — Luster or Museum quality art paper. Perfect if you already have a frame you love or want to frame it yourself. You receive the print only — ready to put in your own frame.

Framed Print — Luster or Museum quality art paper, presented in a frame. Arrives ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping needed. A great all-round choice for well-ventilated bathrooms.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed on canvas and stretched over a wooden frame. No glass, no frame needed — arrives completely ready to hang. The best choice for bathrooms, restrooms, and any damp or high-moisture room, as canvas is naturally moisture-resistant and holds up far better over time.

Paper quality: Luster — A slight sheen that makes colours pop. Versatile, beautiful finish suitable for most interiors.

Paper quality: Museum — A premium matte finish with exceptional colour depth. Ideal if you want the look and feel of a fine-art print.

What is wall art greenery?

Wall art greenery refers to art prints, canvases or framed pieces that feature botanical subjects — leaves, branches, plants or foliage — bringing a sense of nature and calm into your home. The style ranges from loose watercolour botanicals and abstract leaf compositions to more detailed illustrative prints, and it sits comfortably in farmhouse, Scandi, boho and modern-classic interiors alike. It is one of the core expressions of biophilic design, which is all about weaving natural shapes, colours and textures into your living spaces to create a more relaxed and restorative environment. Wall art greenery works particularly well in bathrooms, living rooms, hallways and bedrooms, where the earthy greens and botanical forms introduce a quiet, organic energy without requiring you to maintain a single real plant.

How to Hang and Style Wall Art Greenery in Your Home

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Pick a wall with enough room for all three prints side by side. Measure the wall width and aim for the combined print width to fill roughly two-thirds of it — this creates a balanced, intentional look rather than prints that look lost or crowded.

2. Mark your hanging points at eye level: Eye level is typically around 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print. Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark where each print will sit, keeping an even gap of 5–8 cm between them for a clean, gallery-style arrangement.

3. Match your wall colour to the palette: The greens and ochre tones in botanical greenery art look their best against warm white, off-white, sage or stone walls. Hold a paint swatch next to the print image before you commit — it takes seconds and saves regrets.

4. Choose the right format for the room: For bathrooms or any high-moisture space, opt for the wrapped canvas format as it handles damp conditions far better than paper prints. For living rooms, bedrooms and hallways, Luster or Museum quality paper prints both look excellent.

5. Style with natural accessories: Once hung, bring the look together with a few natural-material accessories nearby — a wooden shelf, a woven basket, a trailing pothos or some dried pampas grass. Botanical wall art and real plants genuinely complement one another beautifully.

Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas — Which Option is Right for You?

Arrives ready to hang — Unframed print: No (you supply your own frame). Framed print: Yes, ready to hang straight away. Wrapped canvas: Yes, ready to hang straight away.

Best for bathrooms and damp rooms — Unframed print: Not recommended. Framed print: Not ideal. Wrapped canvas: Yes — the most moisture-resistant option.

Paper / surface choice — Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: Canvas wrap (no paper option).

aiItems.content:
What are bathroom decor sets?

Bathroom decor sets are coordinated groups of wall art prints — usually sold as a set of 2, 3 or 4 — designed to be hung together in a bathroom for an intentional, pulled-together look. Because every print in the set shares the same colour palette, style and theme, you don't need to do any styling guesswork: they simply work together straight away. A set of 3 like this one is the most popular choice, as it fills a wall beautifully without overwhelming a smaller bathroom space. Choosing a set rather than individual prints also tends to be more cost-effective and saves the time of hunting for pieces that match.

How to Hang Bathroom Decor Sets for the Best Result

1. Measure your wall space first: Hold a piece of paper or tape up to the wall to get a feel for the size before ordering — this is especially important in a bathroom where wall space around tiles, mirrors and cabinets can be limited.

2. Lay the prints out on the floor: Before putting a single nail in the wall, lay all three prints on the floor in the arrangement you plan to hang them. This lets you adjust spacing and confirm the overall width works for your wall.

3. Mark your hanging points at the same height: Use a spirit level and a pencil to mark where each print will hang, keeping them all at the same height. A gap of 5 to 8 cm between prints looks neat and intentional.

4. Hang the centre print first: Start with the middle print so you can balance the other two evenly on either side — this is the easiest way to get a straight, centred result.

5. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back and look from the doorway. Adjust any that need a small tweak — even half a centimetre makes a difference to how professional the final result looks.

Which Option Is Right for Your Bathroom Wall?

Unframed Print — The print arrives rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself in a frame of your choice. Best for those who already have a frame or want full control over the framing style.

Framed Print — Arrives fully assembled and ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping needed. A brilliant time-saving option. Note: for high-humidity bathrooms, canvas is the more moisture-resistant choice.

Wrapped Canvas — The print is stretched over a wooden frame and arrives ready to hang without any frame needed. Canvas is moisture-resistant, making this the recommended option for bathrooms and other damp rooms.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish with a gentle sheen. Colours appear vivid and rich. Works well in well-lit bathrooms.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium matte finish with excellent depth and detail. Suits lower-light or moodier bathroom spaces beautifully.

aiItems.content:
What is a brown painting for home decor?

A brown painting is a piece of artwork — or in this case, a set of wall art prints — where warm brown tones form the dominant colour palette, creating a grounded, earthy feel that suits rustic, natural, and French Country interiors beautifully. Brown-toned art has become increasingly popular in bathrooms and living spaces because it brings warmth without the boldness of brighter colours, working harmoniously with wood, linen, stone, and terracotta. This botanical set features rich, deep brown-black backgrounds with pale cream botanical forms — wild grasses, flowers, leaves, and ferns — giving it a timeless, almost antique quality. How to Hang a Brown Painting Set of 3 in Your Bathroom

1. Choose your wall: Pick the largest unbroken wall in your bathroom — above a bath, vanity, or a longer stretch of wall beside the door. Make sure there's enough horizontal space to display all three prints side by side comfortably.

2. Measure and mark: Lay all three prints on the floor first to check the overall width. Then measure the centre point of the wall and mark it lightly with a pencil. Work outwards from the centre, leaving an even gap of 5–8 cm between each print for a neat, intentional look.

3. Set the height: Aim to hang the centre of the middle print at eye level — roughly 145–150 cm from the floor. In a bathroom where you spend time seated (e.g. at a low vanity), you might drop this slightly for a more comfortable viewing angle.

4. Consider moisture: In a steamy bathroom, opt for the canvas-wrapped version of these prints, as it handles humidity far better than paper. If you go for a framed paper print, make sure the bathroom is reasonably well ventilated.

5. Step back and check: Once all three are up, stand back and look at the alignment from a distance. A small spirit level while hanging saves a lot of straightening later!

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to place in your own frame. Best if you already have frames at home or want to match a very specific frame style. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Your art print arrives already mounted and framed, ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping needed. A great time-saver. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame — no glass, no paper. This is the best option for bathrooms and other high-moisture rooms, as canvas handles humidity far better than paper prints. Arrives ready to hang.

Luster Paper — A semi-sheen finish that gives the artwork a slightly soft, satiny look. Great for everyday display and suits the warm, rustic tones of this botanical set well.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium fine-art finish with deeper colour richness and sharper tonal contrast — ideal if you want the full impact of the dark brown backgrounds and pale botanical detail in these prints.

Framed Print — Your chosen print mounted and framed, arriving ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping or fuss. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper. Ideal if you want a polished, finished look with minimal effort.

How to Hang Blue Wall Art Prints in a Bathroom

1. Measure your wall first: Before ordering, measure the width of the wall or the space above a bath, basin or towel rail. Aim for the combined width of your three prints (plus gaps) to fill roughly two-thirds of that space for a balanced look.

2. Choose the right format for a damp room: In a bathroom, always go for the canvas-wrapped option — it handles moisture far better than paper prints and will keep looking great for longer. If the prints are for a drier room nearby, Luster or Museum quality paper are both excellent choices.

3. Plan your layout before you put a nail in the wall: Lay all three prints on the floor first to check spacing and arrangement. A consistent gap of 5–8 cm between each print looks clean and intentional. Use a spirit level to keep everything straight.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of each print should sit at roughly 145–150 cm from the floor — this is the standard 'eye level' hang height and almost always looks right. If you're hanging them above a piece of furniture, leave at least 15–20 cm of space between the top of the furniture and the bottom of the prints.

5. Step back and adjust: Once they're up, step back and check from the doorway. Small adjustments now make a big difference to the overall feel of the room.

Choosing Your Blue Wall Art Print Format — What's the Difference?

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A high-quality, slightly sheen finish that brings out the depth of the indigo blue beautifully. You choose and add your own frame. Great if you want full control over your framing style. Best for dry rooms.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — A premium matte finish with exceptional colour accuracy and a fine-art feel. Ideal if you want the richest reproduction of the cyanotype tones. Best for dry rooms; you add your own frame.

Framed Print — Your chosen paper print comes ready-mounted and framed, so it arrives completely ready to hang — no hunting for a frame that fits. A real time-saver and looks polished straight out of the box. Best for dry or low-humidity rooms.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden frame — no glass, no paper. This is the best option for bathrooms and other damp or high-moisture rooms, as canvas handles humidity far better than paper. Arrives ready to hang and has a lovely, tactile quality.

This is the moisture-resistant option and our top recommendation for bathrooms and laundry rooms where steam and humidity are a factor. Paper Quality: Luster — A gentle semi-sheen finish that adds a subtle brightness to the mink and charcoal tones, making the ink-wash detail stand out beautifully.

aiItems.content:
What is beige wall art?

Beige wall art refers to art prints, canvases or illustrations that feature beige as a dominant or background colour, creating a warm, neutral and understated look on your walls. It's one of the most versatile choices for home decor because beige works with almost every other colour — from crisp white and charcoal black to sage green and warm terracotta. In interior design, beige wall art is particularly popular in French Country, rustic, botanical and Scandi-inspired schemes where a calm, natural palette is key. Sets of beige art prints are a simple way to create a cohesive, styled look in any room — including bathrooms — without the need for a professional decorator.

How to Hang Beige Wall Art in a Bathroom

1. Measure your wall space first: Before you order, measure the width of the wall where you plan to hang your prints. For a set of 3 in a row, aim for the combined width to fill about two-thirds of the wall — this avoids the prints looking lost or overcrowded.

2. Choose the right finish for damp rooms: In a bathroom, always opt for the canvas-wrapped option if possible, as it handles moisture far better than paper prints. If you prefer framed prints, make sure the room is well ventilated.

3. Mark your hanging points at the same height: Use a spirit level and a pencil to mark where each print will hang. Keep the top edges or centre points at the same height across all three prints for a clean, gallery-style look.

4. Space them evenly: Leave a consistent gap of 5–8 cm between each print. Equal spacing makes the set look deliberate and polished rather than accidental.

5. Step back and check before fixing: Hold the prints up (or use paper templates cut to size) and check the arrangement from the doorway before putting any nails or fixings in. It takes two minutes and saves a lot of replastering.

Choosing Between Unframed, Framed and Canvas-Wrapped Beige Wall Art

Ready to hang — Unframed print: No, you'll need to source your own frame. Framed print: Yes, arrives ready to hang. Wrapped canvas: Yes, arrives ready to hang.

Best for bathrooms / damp rooms — Unframed print: Not ideal — paper is sensitive to moisture. Framed print: Better, especially in well-ventilated rooms. Wrapped canvas: Best choice — most moisture-resistant option.

Paper / finish options — Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: Canvas wrap (no paper choice needed).

Flexibility to reframe — Unframed print: Yes — choose your own frame style and colour. Framed print: No additional framing needed. Wrapped canvas: No frame required; clean contemporary look.

Ideal for — Unframed print: Buyers who already have frames or love a specific frame style. Framed print: Anyone who wants a complete, finished look straight away. Wrapped canvas: Bathrooms, kitchens, high-moisture rooms, or a frameless modern look.

aiItems.content:
What is flowers art?

Flowers art refers to wall art prints and artwork that feature floral subjects — from loose botanical illustrations and watercolour blooms to detailed botanical studies and charming flower shop scenes like this set. It is one of the most popular categories in home décor because florals suit almost every interior style, from country cottage and farmhouse to modern and Scandi. A set of flowers art prints brings colour, life and a personal touch to any room without requiring much decorating skill to pull off. Whether you choose a single statement print or a coordinated set of three, flowers art is an easy, affordable way to refresh a wall and make a space feel properly finished.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Flowers Art Prints in a Bathroom

1. Measure your wall first: Hold a piece of paper or use masking tape on the wall to mark out the rough footprint of all three prints side by side, with a gap of around 5–8 cm between each. Step back and check you're happy with the spacing before you put a single nail in.

2. Find your centre point: Measure the total width of your arrangement and mark the centre on the wall. Hang the middle print first, centred on that mark at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print). This gives you a solid anchor to work from.

3. Hang the outer prints: Work outward from the centre print, keeping the tops of all three prints level with each other. A spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone makes this quick and easy.

4. Choose the right fixings for your wall: For tiled bathroom walls, use adhesive picture-hanging strips rated for your print size — no drilling needed and no damage to tiles. For plasterboard or plaster walls, a small picture hook or nail is fine.

5. Step back and enjoy: Once all three are up, stand back and check the spacing looks even from a distance. A small adjustment at this stage is much easier than you think — and once they're straight, you'll wonder why you didn't do it sooner.

Flowers Art Prints — Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A great choice if you already have a frame you love or want to frame it yourself. Luster paper gives a gentle sheen that brings out the soft watercolour tones beautifully. Best for dry rooms.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The premium paper option — a heavier, fine-art feel with a smooth matte finish that really suits botanical illustration styles like this one. Ideal if you want to frame it in something special. Best for dry rooms.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping, no guesswork on frame fit. A brilliant time-saver and makes a lovely gift. Available in multiple sizes. Best for dry rooms.

Wrapped Canvas — The best choice for bathrooms and other damp or high-moisture rooms. The canvas is moisture-resistant, has a tactile, gallery feel, and arrives ready to hang. No frame needed — the image wraps neatly around the edges for a clean, contemporary look.

aiItems.content:
What are pictures for the bedroom?

Pictures for the bedroom are wall art prints chosen specifically to suit the scale, mood and colour palette of a bedroom space. They typically feature calming, personal or atmospheric subjects — such as coastal scenes, botanicals or abstract art — that help set a relaxing and characterful tone in a room where you start and end each day. A set of three coordinating prints, like this Mediterranean coastal collection, is a popular choice because the trio fills a wall above a headboard naturally and creates a cohesive look without requiring any interior-design expertise. Bedroom wall art is available as unframed prints, ready-to-hang framed prints, or wrapped canvas, so you can choose the format that best suits your walls and your style.

How to Hang Pictures for the Bedroom: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and position: Decide where the prints will go — above the bed headboard is the most popular spot. Measure the width of your headboard or bed and aim for your set of three prints to span roughly two-thirds of that width for a balanced look.

2. Decide on spacing: Lay all three prints out on the floor first to get a feel for the arrangement. A gap of 5–8 cm between each print works well for a set of three — close enough to read as a group, far enough apart to give each piece room to breathe.

3. Find the right height: The centre of your prints should sit at roughly eye level when you're standing — usually around 145–150 cm from the floor. Above a headboard, aim for a 10–15 cm gap between the top of the headboard and the bottom of the prints so they feel connected to the bed rather than floating on the wall.

4. Mark and hang: Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark your hanging points lightly on the wall. If your prints are framed and arrive ready to hang, simply align each hook and you're done. Step back and adjust if needed before making any holes permanent.

5. Style around the prints: Once hung, bring in a few accessories in complementary colours — soft blue or white cushions, a wicker lamp, a terracotta vase — to tie the coastal Mediterranean mood of the prints into the rest of the room.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Our Bedroom Wall Art Print Formats

Format — Unframed Print: The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have a frame you love or want to choose your own to match your bedroom decor exactly.

Format — Framed Print: Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. A brilliant choice if you want the finished look immediately with no fuss.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The print is stretched over a wooden frame with the image wrapping around the edges. No glass, no frame required — just hang and enjoy. Works especially well in relaxed, coastal or natural-texture bedrooms.

Paper finish — Luster Art Paper: A subtle semi-sheen finish that makes colours vivid and fresh. A versatile all-rounder that suits most bedroom styles and lighting conditions.

Paper finish — Museum Quality Paper: A premium fine-art paper with a smooth matte finish and exceptional colour depth. Ideal if your bedroom gets plenty of natural light or if you want the most gallery-worthy result possible.

aiItems.content:
What is beach artwork?

Beach artwork is any printed or painted art that captures coastal scenes, seaside landscapes, ocean views or beach-inspired subjects — think crashing waves, sandy shores, harbour towns, boats and al fresco dining by the sea. It is one of the most popular choices for bringing a relaxed, holiday feeling into the home, and works equally well in bedrooms, living rooms and bathrooms. At AboutWallArt our beach artwork is printed on high-quality art paper or canvas using fade-resistant pigment inks, so the colours stay fresh and vivid for years. The style ranges from loose watercolour sketches and botanical coastal prints to bold abstract ocean photography, so there is something to suit every taste and interior.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Beach Artwork Prints in a Bedroom

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Find a wall with enough horizontal space for all three prints side by side — above a bed headboard or on a feature wall works brilliantly. Measure the width of the wall and divide evenly to work out your print sizes and gaps (5–8 cm between each print is a good rule of thumb).

2. Plan your layout before you put a nail in: Lay the three prints on the floor in front of the wall first. Decide whether you want a straight horizontal row (clean and gallery-like) or a gentle arch with the centre print raised slightly (more relaxed and playful). Take a photo of your layout so you have a reference when you start hanging.

3. Mark your hanging points at the right height: The centre of your art should sit roughly at eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor — or just above the headboard if hanging above a bed. Use a spirit level and a pencil to mark your nail points lightly on the wall before committing.

4. Hang from the centre outwards: Start with the middle print first so you can balance the other two evenly on either side. Step back after each print to check alignment before hanging the next.

5. Style around the prints: Once they are up, add complementary textures nearby — a linen throw, a rattan lampshade or a small coastal ceramic — to pull the Mediterranean mood through the whole room without overcrowding the wall.

Choosing the Right Format for Your Beach Artwork Prints

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love or want to choose your own mount colour. Available on Luster art paper (a gentle sheen, makes blues and whites feel fresh) or Museum quality paper (fully matte, softer gallery finish).

Framed Print — Your art prints arrive already mounted and framed, ready to hang straight out of the box — no trips to a framer needed. The most convenient option if you want a polished, finished look immediately. Available in multiple sizes on Luster or Museum quality paper.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched around a wooden frame, with no glass and no additional frame required. Gives a painterly, textured feel that suits the loose watercolour style of these Amalfi Coast scenes beautifully. Ready to hang and available in multiple sizes.

Paper finish: Luster vs Museum — Luster art paper has a subtle sheen that makes coastal blues feel vivid and luminous — ideal for bright rooms. Museum quality paper is fully matte with a softer, more understated result — ideal if you prefer a traditional gallery feel or your room has strong directional light.

aiItems.content:
What are bedroom prints?

Bedroom prints are wall art prints designed and chosen specifically to suit the mood, scale and décor of a bedroom space. They are typically printed on art paper or canvas and are available unframed, framed or canvas-wrapped so they can be hung directly on the wall. A set of bedroom prints — like this set of 3 — is a popular choice because it creates a curated, gallery-style look above a bed or on a feature wall without requiring any interior-design expertise. The right set of bedroom prints can set the entire tone of a room, bringing colour, personality and a sense of calm or warmth to the space you wake up in every day.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Bedroom Prints for the Best Result

1. Measure your wall space first: Hold a tape measure across the wall above your bed or headboard and note the width. The three prints together should fill roughly two-thirds of that space for a balanced, intentional look — not so wide they feel cramped, not so narrow they look lost.

2. Mark your centre point: Find the centre of your wall space and work outwards. The middle print should sit at the centre, with the left and right prints spaced evenly on either side — around 5 to 8 cm apart is ideal for a set like this to read as a cohesive group.

3. Set your hanging height: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level, or about 15–20 cm above the top of a headboard. Use a spirit level or the free digital level on your phone to keep all three perfectly aligned horizontally.

4. Use the right fixings: For lighter unframed prints in a frame you have chosen, picture hooks or adhesive strips work well. For heavier framed options, use wall plugs and hooks appropriate to your wall type — plasterboard or solid brick will each need different fixings.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back to the doorway and check the spacing and height with fresh eyes. Small adjustments at this stage make a big difference to the finished look.

Choosing Your Format: Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas?

Unframed Print — Printed on your choice of Luster or Museum quality art paper. You choose and source your own frame, giving you full control over the frame colour and style to match your existing bedroom décor. Best for those who already have frames in mind or prefer a DIY approach.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no hunting for frames that fit. Printed on Luster or Museum quality art paper and presented in a frame, saving you time and effort. Ideal if you want a finished, polished look with no extra work.

Wrapped Canvas — The print is stretched and wrapped around a wooden frame, giving a painterly, tactile depth with no glass. No frame or additional hanging hardware needed — arrives ready to go on the wall. A great choice for a relaxed, bohemian or coastal bedroom style. Available in canvas-specific size options.

Paper finish: Luster — A subtle sheen that makes colours — particularly the soft blues, pinks and greens in this coastal set — vivid and bright. Easy to clean and very popular for illustrative and watercolour-style artwork.

Paper finish: Museum Quality — A fine-art matt finish with no sheen, giving the artwork the look and feel of an original painting or fine-art print. Beautifully textured and ideal if you prefer an understated, gallery-style aesthetic.

Choosing the Right Size and Finish for Your Wall

Before you pick a size, I always suggest measuring the wall or the piece of furniture the prints will hang above — a good rule of thumb is that your total grouping should span roughly two-thirds the width of the furniture below it. If you are hanging above a standard double bed, medium to large sizes tend to look most balanced; for a smaller bedroom or a feature wall nook, the smaller sizes are just right and keep things feeling considered rather than crowded.

For finish, Luster paper gives you a lovely slight sheen that makes the greens really pop — great in a brighter room. If your bedroom is on the darker or cosier side, Museum quality paper's matt finish can actually give the colours a beautiful depth, and it avoids any glare from lamps or overhead lights. Both options carry the colours and fine botanical linework in these prints really faithfully. Scroll down to see how each size looks in a bedroom before you decide.

aiItems.content:
What is leaves artwork?

Leaves artwork is a style of wall art that features botanical leaf illustrations, watercolour paintings or printed designs as the central subject. It sits within the broader world of nature-inspired and biophilic interior design, bringing the calm, organic feel of the outdoors into any room. Leaves artwork ranges from simple single-stem studies to layered, painterly compositions like this watercolour set, and it suits a wide variety of interior styles from farmhouse and Scandi to contemporary and boho. It is one of the most popular choices for bedrooms, living rooms and hallways because the natural tones — greens, ochres, whites and earthy neutrals — work with almost any existing colour scheme.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Leaves Artwork Prints in a Bedroom

1. Measure your wall space: Before you put a single nail in, measure the width of the wall or the furniture piece you are hanging above — aim for your total grouping to span about two-thirds of that width for a balanced, considered look.

2. Map it out first: Cut three pieces of paper to your chosen print size and use masking tape to place them on the wall before you commit. This lets you adjust the spacing and height without any unnecessary holes — a gap of around 5 to 8 cm between each print is a great starting point for a clean, gallery-style row.

3. Find the right height: The centre of your grouping should sit roughly at eye level — about 145 to 150 cm from the floor is the standard guide. If you are hanging above a bed or sideboard, keep the bottom edge of the lowest print at least 20 cm above the furniture so it feels intentional rather than crowded.

4. Hang in order from the centre out: Start with the middle print, make sure it is level, then work outwards to the left and right prints — use a spirit level or the bubble level on your phone to keep everything straight.

5. Step back and enjoy: Once all three are up, step back and check the overall balance. If anything feels slightly off, small adjustments now are much easier than after you have fully decorated around them.

Choosing Your Print Option — What Is the Difference?

Unframed Print — You receive the art print only, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have a frame you love or want to match an existing style at home. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — The print arrives already mounted and framed, ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra shopping or fuss. A real time-saver. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame — no glass, no mount, just a clean contemporary look that suits a more relaxed or boho-farmhouse feel. Arrives ready to hang.

Luster Paper — A slight sheen finish that makes colours vivid and rich — brilliant if your bedroom gets good natural light and you want the greens and ochres in this set to really sing.

Museum Quality Paper — A smooth, matt finish with excellent colour depth and no glare — ideal for cosier, lamp-lit bedrooms or if you prefer a more understated, gallery-style look for your botanical prints.

An abstract painting art print is a high-quality reproduction of an original abstract artwork, printed onto art paper or canvas so you can display bold, expressive art in your home without the original price tag. Rather than depicting recognisable scenes or objects, abstract art uses shape, line, tone and texture to create mood and visual interest — like the sweeping charcoal wave forms in this set of three. The prints are produced digitally from the original artwork file, meaning every detail — from the finest hatched linework to the deepest charcoal shadow — is faithfully captured. They're a brilliant way to introduce considered, gallery-style art to any room in your home.

How to Hang an Abstract Painting Art Print Set of 3 in a Bedroom

2. Choose your layout: A straight horizontal row at the same height is the most popular choice for a set of three — clean, modern and easy to execute. Use a spirit level and a pencil to mark the hanging points before you commit.

3. Space them evenly: Aim for a consistent gap of 5–8 cm between each print. Cut a small piece of card to that width and use it as a spacer as you work along the wall — it keeps everything perfectly even.

What are bedroom wall frames?

Bedroom wall frames are art prints displayed in a frame and hung on the wall to decorate a bedroom, adding colour, personality and a finished look to the space. They come in sets — like this set of 3 — or as single pieces, and are available in a range of sizes to suit everything from a small accent wall to a full feature wall above a bed. You can choose framed prints that arrive ready to hang straight away, or unframed prints if you prefer to use your own frames. At AboutWallArt, bedroom wall frames are available in multiple sizes, in Luster or Museum quality paper, and also as wrapped canvas prints — so you can find exactly the right look for your room.

How to Hang Bedroom Wall Frames in 5 Simple Steps

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Decide where you want to hang the prints — above the bed is the most popular spot. Measure the width of the space and divide by the number of prints (3) plus the gaps between them to work out where each print should sit.

2. Cut paper templates: Cut three pieces of paper or card to the size of your chosen prints. Tape them to the wall with masking tape so you can stand back and check the layout before making any holes.

3. Mark your hanging points: Once you're happy with the position, mark the top centre of each template lightly with a pencil. Measure down to find the hanging hook position on the back of each frame and mark those points on the wall.

4. Fix your hooks or picture nails: Use picture nails, adhesive strips or D-ring hooks depending on your wall type. For heavier framed prints, a proper picture nail into a wall plug gives the most secure hold.

5. Hang, level and step back: Hang each print, use a small spirit level to check they're straight, then adjust the gaps so they're even. Step back across the room to check the overall effect — small tweaks at this stage make a big difference to the finished look.

Choosing Your Bedroom Wall Frames Format: Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print — The print is delivered on its own (Luster or Museum quality paper). Great if you already have frames you love or want to choose your own. Most affordable option. You will need to source and fit a frame yourself.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the packaging — no extra shopping or hassle. Available in multiple sizes with a choice of Luster or Museum quality paper. Ideal if you want a neat, complete look without the effort of framing.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a contemporary, frameless look. Arrives ready to hang. No paper or glass — just the printed canvas. Perfect for a more relaxed, modern or boho bedroom style.

Paper Quality: Luster — A semi-gloss finish that brings out colours vibrantly with a slight sheen. Handles reflections better than high-gloss. A brilliant all-round choice for most bedrooms.

Paper Quality: Museum — A fine-art matte finish favoured for high-detail, painterly or illustrated artwork like this London set. No glare, rich depth of tone, and a premium feel. Ideal if you want the closest look to an original illustration.

What are bedroom framed pictures?

Bedroom framed pictures are art prints or illustrations sold ready to display in a bedroom, either unframed, in a frame, or wrapped on canvas — giving you a finished look on your walls without any extra effort. How to Hang Bedroom Framed Pictures in 5 Simple Steps

1. Choose your wall space: Decide where you want to hang your prints — above the headboard is the most popular spot, but a chimney breast, an alcove, or the wall opposite the bed all work well too.

2. Pick your size: Hold a piece of paper or a magazine up to the wall to get a rough feel for scale. For a set of 3 above a double or king-size bed, medium to large prints usually give the best balance.

4. Mark your hanging points: Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark where each hook or nail will go. Getting this step right saves a lot of fiddling later.

Unframed Print — The art print on its own, ready for you to frame however you like. Great if you have a specific frame style in mind or want to match existing frames in your bedroom. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper.

aiItems.content:
What are bedroom wall picture frames?

Bedroom wall picture frames are frames — or framed art prints — chosen specifically to display artwork on bedroom walls, creating a cohesive, decorative look in your personal space. They come in a range of sizes, finishes and formats, from simple unframed prints you mount yourself to fully framed pieces that arrive ready to hang. A well-chosen set of bedroom wall picture frames can tie together a room's colour palette, reflect your personality and make an otherwise plain wall feel thoughtfully designed. Sets of three are especially popular in bedrooms because they create a balanced, gallery-style arrangement above a bed or on a feature wall without requiring any design experience to pull off.

How to Hang Bedroom Wall Picture Frames in a Row Above Your Bed

1. Measure your wall space: Start by measuring the width of your bed or headboard. For a balanced look, aim for your set of three prints to span roughly two-thirds of that width in total — this stops them looking too cramped or too spread out.

2. Find your centre point: Mark the centre of the wall lightly with a pencil. This is where the middle print will sit, so the whole arrangement is perfectly symmetrical above the bed.

3. Set your hanging height: The centre of the middle print should sit approximately 15–20 cm above the top of your headboard (or about 145–150 cm from the floor if there is no headboard). This keeps the art visually connected to the bed rather than floating high up on the wall.

4. Space the prints evenly: Keep a consistent gap of 5–8 cm between each print. Cut small paper spacers to the same width and hold them between the prints as you mark your fixing points — this is a quick trick that guarantees even spacing every time.

5. Use a spirit level: Before you put in any nails or fixings, hold each print up and use a small spirit level (or the free level tool on your phone) to make sure they are perfectly horizontal. Even a tiny tilt is very noticeable once the prints are up.

Choosing Your Format: Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas?

Unframed Print — The print is supplied on its own (Luster or Museum quality art paper). Great if you already have frames you love or want to choose your own — and it keeps the cost down. You will need to source and fit a frame yourself before hanging.

Framed Print — The art print comes ready-assembled in a frame, so it arrives ready to hang straight away with no extra shopping or effort. Perfect if you want a polished, finished look without the hassle. Available in multiple sizes with Luster or Museum quality paper options.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary gallery feel with no glass and no additional frame needed. It arrives ready to hang and suits a more relaxed, modern bedroom aesthetic. Available in a range of canvas sizes.

Paper Quality: Luster — A semi-sheen finish that reduces glare while keeping colours vibrant and rich. A great all-rounder for most bedroom settings and lighting conditions.

Paper Quality: Museum — A fine-art matt finish with exceptional colour depth and a premium, gallery-quality feel. Ideal if you want the prints to look truly special and last for many years.

aiItems.content:
What is a travel poster?

A travel poster is a decorative art print that celebrates a specific city, landmark, or destination — typically using bold imagery, illustrative or watercolour artwork, and a strong sense of place and atmosphere. Originally used in the early 20th century to promote rail and air travel, the style has evolved into one of the most popular forms of home wall art, loved for its ability to bring a sense of wanderlust and personality to any room. Today's travel poster art prints range from vintage-inspired retro designs to modern watercolour and minimalist styles, making them a versatile choice for bedrooms, living rooms, and hallways. A set of travel poster prints — like this New York trio — works especially well as a curated gallery wall that tells a visual story of a place you love.

How to Hang a Travel Poster Set of 3 in Your Bedroom

1. Measure your wall space first: Use a tape measure to find the total width available. For a set of 3, allow for a 3–5 cm gap between each print and check the combined width fits comfortably between any furniture or door frames.

2. Choose your layout: A straight horizontal row at eye level is the most classic and impactful arrangement for a set of 3. Alternatively, a slight staggered or stepped layout adds a more relaxed, gallery feel — great if your bedroom has an asymmetric wall or sloped ceiling.

3. Mark your hanging points in pencil: Hold each print up in position and lightly mark the top centre of each with a pencil. Using a spirit level across all three marks ensures they sit evenly — a small level tool is a worthwhile investment for any gallery wall.

4. Hang the centre print first: Starting from the middle and working outwards helps you keep the arrangement symmetrical. Use the gap measurement you decided on to position the left and right prints evenly from the centre one.

5. Step back and check before you commit: Once all three are up, step right back to the other side of the room and check the alignment at a distance — small adjustments at this stage are much easier than after you've filled the pencil marks.

Which Option is Right for You? Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas

Unframed Print — You receive the art print only, printed on your choice of Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Perfect if you already have frames you love, or if you want to choose your own framing to match your existing bedroom décor. Available in a wide range of sizes.

Framed Print — Your art print arrives ready to hang in a frame — no extra shopping or hassle required. A brilliant option if you want a polished, finished look straight out of the box. Available with a choice of Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary gallery-style finish with no glass. Arrives ready to hang and adds a tactile, painterly feel to the New York autumn scenes. Available in a range of size options.

Paper Finish: Luster vs Museum Quality — Luster art paper has a gentle sheen that makes colours like the warm ochre and amber tones in this set feel vibrant and rich. Museum quality paper is a fine-art matte finish with a softer, more understated look — ideal if your bedroom has bright natural light or you prefer a gallery-wall aesthetic without any glare.

aiItems.content:
What is autumn artwork?

Autumn artwork is any artwork — print, painting, illustration or photograph — that captures the colours, scenes and mood of the autumn season, typically featuring warm tones of orange, coral, amber and red alongside earthy greens and greys. It's a popular choice for home decor because those seasonal hues are naturally warm and inviting, making any room feel cosier and more personal. Autumn artwork can range from abstract seasonal colour-field pieces to detailed illustrative scenes like cityscapes, woodland landscapes or market stalls draped in harvest produce. Sets of matching autumn art prints are especially popular for creating a cohesive gallery wall that brings a seasonal, travel or botanical story together in one go.

How to Hang Autumn Artwork in a Bedroom

1. Plan your layout first: Cut pieces of paper to your chosen print size and use painter's tape to map out the arrangement on your wall before you put a single nail in. For a set of three, a straight horizontal row works brilliantly above a bed — aim for a total width roughly two-thirds of your bed's headboard width so it sits in proportion.

2. Find the right hanging height: The centre of the middle print should sit at roughly eye level when you're standing — around 145–150 cm from the floor is the standard. If you're hanging above a bed or a piece of furniture, leave about 15–20 cm of breathing room between the top of the furniture and the bottom of the prints.

3. Space the prints evenly: For a set of three, a gap of 5–8 cm between each print looks clean and intentional without feeling too cramped or too spread out. Use a tape measure and a spirit level — even a small angle can be noticeable once you step back.

4. Choose your fixing: For lightweight unframed prints in a clip frame or poster frame, adhesive picture strips work a treat and won't damage the wall. For heavier framed prints, use a proper picture hook rated for the weight. The framed option arrives ready to hang, so you just need to find your fixing point and you're done.

5. Step back and enjoy: Once they're up, step back to the opposite side of the room to check the balance. Autumn prints with warm coral and grey tones look especially good caught in natural daylight, so if possible position them on a wall that gets some daytime light.

Choosing Your Autumn Artwork Format — What's the Difference?

Format — Unframed Print: the printed art only, no frame included — ideal if you already have a frame or prefer to choose your own mount and framing style at home.

Format — Framed Print: the art is printed and supplied in a frame, arriving ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra shopping required.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: the artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched around a wooden frame, giving a gallery-style finish with no frame or glass needed — also arrives ready to hang.

Paper choice (prints only) — Luster Art Paper: a semi-gloss finish that makes warm tones like coral and amber really vibrant — great for rooms with natural light.

Paper choice (prints only) — Museum Quality Paper: a fine-art matte finish with a premium feel — ideal for a quieter, gallery-style look where you want the illustration to speak for itself without any surface sheen.

Ready to hang — Unframed Print: No (print only; you source and fit your own frame).

Ready to hang — Framed Print and Wrapped Canvas: Yes — both options arrive fully ready to hang, saving time and effort.

aiItems.content:
What is master bedroom art above bed?

Master bedroom art above bed refers to wall art prints hung directly above the headboard as the main focal point of the room. It is typically a set of prints — often two or three — arranged in a row or symmetrical grouping to anchor the bed within the space. The artwork sits roughly 15 to 25 cm above the headboard and spans a width proportionate to the bed beneath it, creating a cohesive, designed feel. Done well, it replaces the need for additional wall décor and gives the whole room a sense of calm, intention and personality.

How to Hang Master Bedroom Art Above Bed: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your headboard width: Start by measuring the width of your headboard. Your three prints should span roughly 60–75% of that width in total (including the gaps between them) for a balanced, proportionate look.

2. Choose your print size: For a king or super-king bed, A3 prints or larger tend to work best. For a double, A4 or A3 are ideal. Use the size-guide image below the product to see how each size looks in a real bedroom setting before ordering.

3. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall space above the headboard and mark it lightly with a pencil. Your middle print should be centred on this point.

4. Decide on your gaps: A gap of 5 to 8 cm between each print looks clean and intentional. Measure and mark the hanging points for the left and right prints working outward from the centre.

5. Hang at the right height: Position the bottom edge of your prints roughly 15 to 25 cm above the top of the headboard — close enough to feel connected to the bed, not floating up the wall.

6. Step back and check: Before making permanent holes, hold the prints in place (or use paper templates cut to size) and step back to check the spacing and height from across the room. Adjust as needed, then hang with confidence.

Choosing the Right Print Option for Your Bedroom

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love or want to match existing décor exactly. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no need to source a frame. A fantastic time-saver and the most popular choice for above-the-bed displays. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, across multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame — no glass, no additional framing needed. Arrives ready to hang and gives a softer, more textural feel that suits the watercolour style of this set beautifully. Available in multiple sizes.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish that gives a gentle sheen and makes colours pop. Works really well in bedrooms where there is some natural light hitting the wall.

Museum Quality Paper — A fine-art matte finish that renders the soft watercolour tones of this winter New York set with exceptional depth and subtlety. Ideal if you want the most faithful, gallery-feel reproduction of the artwork.

aiItems.content:
What are French Posters?

French posters are decorative wall art prints inspired by the culture, landmarks, and romantic atmosphere of France — most commonly featuring iconic imagery such as the Eiffel Tower, Parisian street scenes, cafés, bicycles, and vintage travel themes. They typically use a warm, illustrated or painterly style with soft colour palettes of white, green, red, and gold tones that give them a timeless, charming quality. French posters have been popular since the late 19th century when artists like Toulouse-Lautrec created bold, colourful prints for theatre and travel advertising in Paris. Today, modern french posters range from faithful reproductions of vintage originals to fresh, contemporary watercolour illustrations perfect for home décor. They are a go-to choice for adding a touch of Parisian style and travel-inspired warmth to bedrooms, living rooms, and hallways.

How to Hang French Posters as a Set of 3

1. Plan your layout first: Lay the three prints on the floor in front of the wall you have in mind. Arrange them in a horizontal row and step back to check the spacing feels balanced — a gap of around 5–8 cm between each print usually looks just right.

2. Find your centre point: Measure the total width of all three prints plus your gaps, then find the midpoint of your wall. Mark this lightly with a pencil so you can work outward symmetrically from the centre.

3. Set your hanging height: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor works well in most rooms. If you're hanging above a bed or furniture, aim for the bottom of the prints to sit about 20–25 cm above the top of the piece below.

4. Use a spirit level: A small spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone makes all the difference — even a slight tilt is very noticeable once the prints are up. Mark your nail positions lightly before committing.

5. Hang and stand back: Once all three are up, stand back from across the room and check the overall look. Small adjustments now save a lot of re-hanging later — and enjoy your little piece of Paris!

Choosing Your French Posters Format — Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — Great if you already have frames you love or want full control over your framing style. Luster paper gives a gentle sheen and clean, bright colour. You select your frame separately.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The best choice if you want the richest, most gallery-worthy result. Museum paper has a beautiful fine-art matt finish that suits the delicate watercolour illustration style of these Parisian prints perfectly. You select your frame separately.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum paper) — Arrives completely ready to hang with no extra steps needed — ideal if you want a polished, finished look straight away and don't want to spend time sourcing a frame. Available in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, so there is no need for any framing at all. Gives a relaxed, contemporary feel and arrives ready to hang. A great option if you want the set to feel more casual and modern rather than classic and framed.

Posters for bedroom are decorative wall art prints sized and styled to suit a bedroom setting — typically sold as individual prints or coordinated sets that bring colour, personality, and a sense of calm or style to your sleeping space. How to Hang Posters for Bedroom — a Simple Step-by-Step

1. Measure your wall space first: Use a tape measure to note the width and height of the area you want to fill — above the bed, on a feature wall, or along a hallway leading into the room. This tells you which print sizes will fit comfortably without looking lost or overcrowded.

2. Choose your size and finish: Select your preferred size from the product options. Opt for Luster paper if your bedroom gets good natural light, or Museum quality matte paper for a softer, more intimate look in cosier spaces. aiItems.content:
What is Paris wall art?

Paris wall art refers to printed artwork, illustrations or photography that celebrates the city of Paris — its iconic landmarks, streets, cafés, architecture and culture. It is a hugely popular style of home décor for anyone who loves travel, French style or simply the romantic, effortlessly chic aesthetic that Paris is famous for. Sets of Paris wall art prints, like this watercolour trio, are particularly popular because they let you create a cohesive gallery-style display in one go. They suit a wide range of rooms and interior styles, from a cosy eclectic bedroom to a clean, minimal living space, making them one of the most versatile and giftable choices in travel-inspired home décor.

How to Hang Paris Wall Art Prints as a Set of 3

1. Plan your layout first: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of the wall where you plan to hang them. This lets you see how the set looks as a group and decide on spacing before you make any holes.

2. Find your centre point: Measure the total width of all three prints plus your chosen gaps between them. Divide this by two to find the centre of the arrangement, and line that up with the centre of your wall or the piece of furniture below (such as a bed headboard or console table).

3. Mark your hanging heights: Use a pencil and spirit level to mark where each hook or nail will go. For a bedroom, aim to hang the prints so the middle of the arrangement sits roughly at eye level when you are sitting up in bed — usually around 120 to 130 cm from the floor.

4. Keep gaps consistent: A gap of 5 to 8 cm between each print looks tidy and intentional. Use a small piece of card cut to that width as a spacer to keep things even as you work across the wall.

5. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back and check they are level and evenly spaced before you are done. Adjust as needed — it only takes a moment and makes all the difference to the finished look.

Choosing Your Paris Wall Art Print Format

Unframed Print — The print is delivered flat and ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have a frame you love or want to choose your own. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Your print arrives already framed and genuinely ready to hang straight away — no extra trips to a frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saving option. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a contemporary, paint-on-canvas feel. No frame or glass required — just hang and enjoy. Available in a range of sizes.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish that keeps colours bright and vivid. A great all-round choice for most rooms and lighting conditions.

Museum Quality Paper — A fine-art paper with a slightly textured, matte feel that really draws out the depth and nuance of watercolour illustration. Ideal if you want the closest feel to an original painting.

Art for bedroom refers to wall art prints and decorative pieces chosen specifically to suit the scale, mood and colour palette of a bedroom space. How to Hang Art for Bedroom Walls: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and layout: Decide whether you want to hang your prints above the bed, on a feature wall, or beside a window. For a set of 3, a horizontal row above the headboard is the most popular and effective arrangement — centre the group over the bed for a balanced, finished look.

3. Hang at the right height: As a general rule, the centre of your artwork grouping should sit at roughly eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor. 4. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back and look at the arrangement from across the room. Adjust any that look slightly off — even a centimetre or two can make a difference. A small spirit level on top of each frame helps get things perfectly straight.

What are vintage travel wall art prints?

Vintage travel wall art prints are illustrated or graphic artworks inspired by the golden age of travel — think hand-drawn cityscapes, romantic European street scenes, Parisian cafés, and the Eiffel Tower rendered in soft, nostalgic colour palettes. They capture the mood of a particular place or era rather than functioning as a literal photograph, giving them a timeless, story-rich quality that suits a wide range of interiors. This set of three features charming watercolour-style illustrations of Parisian boutique streets complete with cosy café awnings, bistro chairs, and the iconic Eiffel Tower, all in a warm palette of white, beige, burgundy, and black. Vintage travel prints are especially popular in bedrooms, where they add a personal, well-travelled feel without overwhelming the space. They suit anyone who loves French style, boutique Parisien aesthetics, or simply the romance of European city life.

How to Hang Vintage Travel Art Prints as a Set of 3

1. Choose your layout: The most popular approach is a straight horizontal row — all three prints lined up at the same height with equal gaps (around 5–8 cm works well). This feels clean and intentional. If your wall is taller than it is wide, try a staggered arrangement with the centre print slightly higher for a relaxed gallery feel.

2. Find the right height: Aim to centre the middle print at roughly eye level — about 145–150 cm from the floor to the middle of the print. If you're hanging above a bed, leave around 20–25 cm between the top of the headboard and the bottom of the lowest print so it doesn't feel cramped.

3. Mark your spots before you drill: Cut paper templates to the size of each print and use low-tack masking tape to stick them on the wall first. Step back, adjust until you're happy, then mark through the templates. This saves a lot of unnecessary holes in the wall.

4. Use a spirit level: Even if it looks straight to the eye, a small spirit level across the top of all three prints after hanging will make sure they're perfectly aligned — especially important with a set of three where any tilt is easy to spot.

5. Stand back and enjoy: Once they're up, give yourself a moment to take them in from the doorway. That's the true test of whether the arrangement works — and with a set this lovely, we think you'll be very pleased.

Unframed print on Luster art paper — A versatile option if you already have frames you love or want to source your own. Luster paper gives a gentle sheen that makes the warm burgundy and beige tones in these Parisian illustrations really pop. Great value and easy to post or gift.

Unframed print on Museum quality paper — A matte, gallery-style finish that suits the hand-illustrated, watercolour feel of this artwork beautifully. Slightly more texture than Luster, giving a fine-art feel. Choose this if you prefer a softer, non-reflective look on your wall.

Framed print — Arrives fully assembled and ready to hang straight away — no searching for a frame that fits. Ideal if you want the complete, finished look without any extra effort. The clean framing complements the crisp white and beige backgrounds of these Parisian prints perfectly.

Wrapped canvas — The artwork is printed and wrapped around a solid wooden stretcher frame, giving a painterly, gallery-canvas feel. No frame needed. This option adds lovely texture and depth to the hand-illustrated style of these prints, and suits a more relaxed, artistic bedroom aesthetic. Also arrives ready to hang.

content.productDescription:
Bring some moody, quiet beauty into your bedroom with this nature art set of three botanical prints. Each piece features delicate white botanical illustrations — wildflowers and meadow stems, a generous blossom branch, and a graceful bare tree — all rendered against a deep, textured charcoal-brown background that has the wonderful worn quality of aged, deckle-edged paper. Together they feel like something discovered in a French country farmhouse, earthy and calm, but genuinely striking on a wall.

What I really love about this set is how the contrast works — those soft, almost ghostly white plants against the rich dark ground give the whole thing a rustic, timeworn feel without being heavy. The brown tones are warm enough to sit beautifully in a bedroom that leans into natural, country or botanical styling, and the three subjects — meadow wildflowers, open blossom, a branching tree — tell a gentle story as a group. It's the kind of art you notice every morning and never get bored of.

What's Included with Nature Art Dark Botanical Wildflowers & Blossom Wall Art Prints | Set of 3

  • A set of 3 individual art prints, each featuring a distinct botanical subject: a wildflower meadow, a flowering blossom branch, and a bare branching tree, all on a deep charcoal-brown textured ground
  • Printed in the UK using fade-resistant pigment inks, designed for indoor display
  • The deckle-edged, aged-paper aesthetic is part of the printed artwork itself — giving each print that authentic rustic character straight out of the box
  • Framed and canvas-wrapped options arrive ready to hang — saving you the time and hassle of hunting for a frame that fits perfectly
  • Choose between unframed and framed options in multiple sizes and in Luster or Museum quality; also available in wrapped canvas size options

How to Style nature art like this in a Bedroom

I'd hang all three in a horizontal row above a bed or a low chest of drawers, spaced evenly with a small gap between each — it's the most natural way to let the trio read as a connected set. Because the prints carry deep charcoal-brown tones, they sit really well against warm white, linen, sage or even dusty blush walls — the contrast is always just right. If you're going for a proper French country bedroom feel, pair them with natural textures: linen bedding, a rattan lamp, aged wood furniture. The botanical subjects bring that countryside, garden-gathered quality that makes a bedroom feel genuinely restful.

For a more contemporary look, you can stagger the three at slightly different heights for a relaxed, gallery-style arrangement — it still works because the shared dark ground ties them together visually. Have a browse of our full botanical wall art collection if you'd like to mix in additional prints around this set.

Choosing the Right Size and Finish for Your Wall

With a dark, high-contrast set like this, going a touch larger than you think you need is almost always the right call — the detail in those fine botanical lines really rewards a bit of space. For above a double or king-size bed, I'd suggest looking at the medium or large size options so the trio fills the wall comfortably without feeling lost. For a smaller bedroom wall or a nook, the smaller sizes are just as lovely and keep the intimate, close-up feel of the artwork intact.

On finish, Museum quality paper gives the richest depth to those dark charcoal-brown tones and makes the white botanical details really pop — ideal if this is going to be the centrepiece of your room. Luster is a brilliant everyday choice too, with a gentle sheen that handles bedroom lighting beautifully. If you'd prefer something with a bit more texture and dimension, the wrapped canvas option is worth considering — that deep ground colour looks wonderful on canvas. Scroll down to see how each size looks in a bedroom before you decide.

aiItems.content:
What is nature art?

Nature art is artwork that draws its subject matter from the natural world — plants, botanicals, trees, flowers, landscapes and wildlife — reproduced as wall art prints for your home. It covers a huge range of styles, from loose watercolour botanicals and rustic country illustrations to dark, moody pressed-plant studies like this set. Nature art is one of the most enduringly popular choices for bedrooms and living spaces because it brings a calm, organic quality to any room without feeling dated. Whether you prefer soft pastels or dramatic dark tones, there is a style of nature art to suit almost every interior.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Nature Art Prints in Your Bedroom

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Pick a wall with enough horizontal space for all three prints side by side — above a bed headboard or a chest of drawers works brilliantly. Measure the total width available and divide by three to work out roughly how wide each print should be, leaving an even gap (around 5–8 cm) between each one.

2. Mark your hanging points at the right height: For a bedroom, aim to hang the centre of the group at roughly eye level when you are sitting up in bed — usually around 130–140 cm from the floor. Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark your hanging points before you put anything on the wall.

3. Start from the middle print and work outward: Hang the centre print first, then use it as your reference to position the left and right prints at exactly the same height. This makes it far easier to keep the trio level and evenly spaced without lots of readjusting.

4. Step back and check the overall balance: Once all three are up, step back to the doorway and look at the group as a whole. The three botanical subjects — wildflowers, blossom, and a branching tree — should read as a calm, connected set. Adjust any that look slightly off before you are fully happy.

Choosing Your Print Option — What's the Difference?

Unframed Print — The art print is supplied on its own, ready for you to frame or display as you choose. Available on Luster art paper (a gentle sheen, great everyday choice) or Museum quality paper (richer colour depth, ideal for statement pieces). You select the size and paper type at checkout.

Framed Print — Your chosen print comes ready to hang in a frame — no need to source a frame separately or worry about whether it will fit. A brilliant time-saver and the finish looks polished straight out of the box. Available in multiple sizes on Luster or Museum quality paper.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a more textural, gallery feel. No glass, no mount — just the art itself. Arrives ready to hang and suits those who prefer a more relaxed, tactile look. Available in a range of wrapped canvas sizes.

Paper finish — Luster vs Museum Quality: Luster art paper has a subtle sheen that handles everyday lighting well and keeps colours looking fresh. Museum quality paper offers a deeper, more archival-grade result with richer contrast — especially noticeable with dark-toned artwork like this botanical set. Both are printed with fade-resistant pigment inks in the UK.

aiItems.content:
What is floral wall art?

Floral wall art refers to printed artwork featuring flowers, botanical stems, or plant-based imagery, designed to be displayed on a wall as a decorative piece. It spans a huge range of styles — from loose watercolour sketches to bold high-contrast photographic studies like this charcoal-and-white botanical set. Floral art prints are one of the most popular choices for bedrooms and living spaces because they bring a sense of nature indoors without any upkeep. A set of 3 floral art prints creates a cohesive gallery-style display that feels intentional and well put together, whether your style leans French Country, contemporary, or somewhere in between.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Floral Wall Art Prints in a Bedroom

1. Measure your wall space: Hold a sheet of paper up to the wall to get a rough sense of scale before committing to a size. For above a double or king bed, aim for a total width that spans roughly two-thirds of the headboard width across all three prints combined.

2. Choose your layout: A straight horizontal row at eye level — or just above headboard height — is the most classic approach for a set of 3. Alternatively, stack them vertically on a narrow wall for a tall, gallery-style feature.

3. Mark equal spacing: Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark the hanging points before you put anything on the wall. Keep gaps between prints consistent — around 5 to 8 cm works well for this size of set.

4. Hang the centre print first: Get the middle print perfectly level, then work outward to the left and right. This keeps the whole row balanced and centred on the wall.

5. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back to the doorway and check alignment from a distance — small adjustments are much easier to spot from across the room than up close.

Floral Wall Art Prints — Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print — The print is delivered flat and ready for you to frame yourself. Ideal if you already have a frame you love or want to match existing décor precisely. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight away — no separate frame hunting needed. A great time-saver and the finish looks polished and complete from day one. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame with the image wrapping around the edges. No frame or glass required — just hang and enjoy. Gives a more relaxed, contemporary feel compared to a framed print.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish with a gentle sheen that adds a touch of vibrancy. Great for everyday display and suits most bedroom lighting conditions well.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium matte finish with exceptional tonal depth — ideal for high-contrast artwork like this charcoal botanical set, where rich deep blacks make a real difference to the overall impact.
