aiItems.content:
What is a floral art wall?

A floral art wall is a curated display of botanical or flower-themed wall art prints grouped together to create a cohesive decorative focal point in a room. It typically features two or more prints arranged in a row, grid, or gallery layout, united by a shared colour palette, style, or plant subject. Floral art walls are especially popular in bedrooms, where calm, nature-inspired imagery helps create a relaxing atmosphere. Cyanotype-style botanical prints — like this indigo and white set of three — are a particularly sought-after choice because their striking contrast and handcrafted feel suit everything from country cottage to contemporary interiors.

How to Hang a Floral Art Wall in Your Bedroom

1. Measure your wall space first: Decide where you want your floral art wall to live — above the bed, on a feature wall, or in an alcove. Measure the width and note any furniture below, as this will guide which print size works best.

2. Choose your set size and finish: For this set of 3, decide whether you'd like unframed prints, framed prints (which arrive ready to hang), or wrapped canvas. Pick Luster art paper for a gentle sheen or Museum quality for a fine-art matte look.

3. Plan your layout before you hang: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of the wall to trial the spacing. A gap of around 5–8 cm between each print looks balanced. Use masking tape on the wall to mark your hanging points before committing to nails.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of the group should sit at roughly eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor works well for most people. If hanging above a headboard, leave a gap of about 15–20 cm between the top of the headboard and the bottom of the prints.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back and check the spacing looks even from across the room. Small adjustments now save a lot of re-hanging later!

Choosing Your Print Option — What's the Difference?

Unframed Print — You receive the art print only, ready for you to frame as you choose. Available on Luster art paper (gentle sheen) or Museum quality paper (fine-art matte). Great if you already have frames or want to choose your own.

Framed Print — Your art print arrives already framed and ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to a frame shop needed. Available in multiple sizes on Luster or Museum quality paper. The easiest, most convenient option for most people.

Wrapped Canvas — The botanical design is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a more textural, gallery-style finish without the need for glass. Arrives ready to hang. Available in a range of canvas sizes.

Paper Finish: Luster — A semi-gloss surface with a gentle sheen that makes colours feel vibrant. Works especially well in rooms with natural light where the indigo tones can really come alive.

Paper Finish: Museum Quality — A smooth, fine-art matte surface with no glare. Ideal for bedrooms with softer, ambient lighting where you want a quieter, more traditional botanical print feel.

And if you want something with real presence and a bit of texture on the wall, the wrapped canvas option is worth considering too. aiItems.content:
What is a floral print?

A floral print is a piece of wall art featuring botanical or flower-based imagery — from loose watercolour blooms to detailed botanical illustrations like the chrysanthemum designs in this set. Floral prints have been a staple of interior decorating for centuries, particularly in French Country and rustic-style homes, where nature-inspired motifs bring warmth and character to a space. Today, floral wall art prints are printed on high-quality art paper or canvas using fade-resistant inks, making them a durable and accessible way to bring the beauty of the natural world indoors. Whether you choose a single statement piece or a coordinated set of three like this one, a floral print instantly adds softness and personality to any room.

How to Hang a Floral Print Set of 3 in Your Bedroom

1. Plan your layout first: Lay all three prints on the floor or a bed to decide on spacing before you pick up a hammer. For a clean, classic look, keep equal gaps between each print — around 5 to 8 cm works well for most sizes.

2. Find your centre point: Measure the total width of all three prints plus your gaps, then find the midpoint of your wall or headboard. Mark this lightly with a pencil — this is where the centre of your middle print will hang.

3. Set the right height: The centre of the middle print should sit roughly at eye level when you're standing, or about 15 to 20 cm above the top of a headboard if you're hanging the set above your bed.

4. Mark and hang one at a time: Start with the centre print, fix it securely, then work outwards to the left and right prints — checking with a spirit level as you go to keep everything straight.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back and view the set as a whole. Small adjustments now are much easier than noticing a wonky print later!

Choosing Your Format: Floral Print Options Compared

Format — Unframed Print: The print only, on your choice of Luster or Museum quality art paper. You select and source your own frame. Great if you have a specific frame in mind or want to match existing décor.

Format — Framed Print: Printed on Luster or Museum quality paper and presented in a frame — arrives ready to hang straight out of the box, no extra effort needed.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame — ready to hang, with a tactile, gallery-style finish and no frame required.

Paper finish (prints only) — Luster art paper: A gentle sheen that brings out contrast and makes colours appear vivid and bright — ideal in well-lit rooms.

Paper finish (prints only) — Museum quality paper: A premium matte finish with excellent depth and detail — beautifully suited to the hand-drawn botanical style of this chrysanthemum set.

Ready to hang? — Unframed: No. Framed: Yes. Wrapped canvas: Yes.

Best for — Unframed: Budget-conscious buyers or those with a specific frame preference. Framed & Canvas: Anyone who wants a completely hassle-free finish straight from delivery.

aiItems.content:
What is a nature painting?

A nature painting is a work of art that depicts subjects from the natural world — such as botanicals, wildflowers, leaves, landscapes or wildlife — rendered in a chosen artistic style, from realistic to abstract. In home décor, nature painting wall art prints are one of the most popular ways to bring an organic, calming feel into a room without the cost of an original canvas. They come in many styles, from soft watercolour florals to dramatic dark-toned botanical studies like this set, and suit a wide range of interiors from French Country and rustic to contemporary and minimalist. Printed nature painting art is also practical: high-quality pigment inks mean the colours stay true for years, and unframed or ready-to-hang framed options make it simple to refresh a room whenever you fancy a change.

How to Hang a Nature Painting Set of 3 in a Bedroom

1. Measure first: Measure the wall space above your bed or chosen wall. Aim for the combined width of all three prints plus your preferred gaps between them (usually 5–10 cm each) to sit within the width of your headboard or bed frame for the most balanced look.

2. Find your centre: Mark the centre point of your wall space lightly in pencil. The middle print should sit centred on this mark. Use a spirit level to keep all three at the same height — eye level when standing (roughly 145–150 cm to the centre of the prints) is a reliable starting point.

3. Space evenly: Keep the gaps between each print consistent — 5 cm to 10 cm works well for a triptych set. Cut paper templates the same size as your prints and tape them to the wall first so you can step back and check the arrangement before making any holes.

4. Hang and check: Hang your prints using the fixings included with framed options, or use picture hooks suitable for your wall type for unframed prints in your own frames. Stand back, check they are level, and adjust as needed. A small piece of museum putty on each bottom corner keeps prints steady and prevents them from tilting over time.

Choosing Your Format: Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas?

Unframed print — The print is supplied on its own (Luster or Museum quality paper), giving you full flexibility to choose your own frame style and colour. Great if you already have frames or want a very specific look. Requires your own framing before hanging.

Framed print — Your art print arrives ready to hang straight away — no need to source a frame that fits. A brilliant time-saver, and the framed options are available in multiple sizes. The dark botanical tones of this set suit both light and dark frame options beautifully.

Wrapped canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a gallery-style finish with no glazing. Ready to hang, with a tactile, paint-like quality that works especially well with the rich dark tones and botanical detail in this set. Available in a range of sizes.

Paper finish: Luster — A semi-sheen finish that enhances depth and colour richness. Works particularly well with the dark brown-black tones of this botanical set, bringing out fine detail in the cream-white botanical forms.

Paper finish: Museum quality — A completely matt, gallery-standard finish for a more understated, sophisticated result. Ideal if your room has significant natural light, as there is no surface sheen to create glare.

A set of bedroom pictures, like a coordinated trio of botanical prints, creates a cohesive look without the effort of sourcing individual pieces that work together. They are available as unframed prints, framed prints ready to hang, or wrapped canvas options to suit different tastes and budgets.

How to Hang Bedroom Pictures: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Decide which wall will display your prints — above the bed is the most popular spot. Measure the width of the wall or the furniture below so you can work out how far apart to space the three prints.

2. Plan your layout before you hang: Lay the three prints out on the floor or a bed first to visualise the arrangement. A straight horizontal row works beautifully for a set of three botanical prints like these. Mark your spacing — around 5–8 cm between each print is a good guide.

3. Find the right hanging height: The centre of each print should sit at roughly eye level when you are standing, or about 15–20 cm above the top of a headboard if hanging above a bed. Use a spirit level to keep them straight.

4. Mark and hang: Lightly mark your nail or hook positions in pencil, double-check they are level, and hang your prints. Step back and adjust as needed. If you have chosen a framed option, it comes ready to hang straight away.

5. Step back and enjoy: Once all three are up and level, take a moment to see how the arrangement feels. Botanical sets like this one look stunning with a small adjustment to even out the spacing — it makes a real difference to the finished look.

Finish — Unframed Print: Clean, flat art paper with a Luster or matte Museum surface. | Framed Print: Neat, presented finish suited to a polished bedroom look. | Wrapped Canvas: Soft, organic texture that suits rustic and French Country interiors particularly well.

aiItems.content:
What is a flower print?

A flower print is a piece of printed wall art featuring floral imagery — whether that's a bold botanical illustration, a delicate watercolour arrangement, or a charming scene like a cottage flower shop. Flower prints are one of the most popular choices for bedroom and living room walls because they bring natural colour and a sense of calm into a space. They come in a huge range of styles, from loose and painterly to crisp and graphic, so there's something to suit almost every home. A set of flower prints — like a coordinated trio — is a particularly easy way to create a gallery wall with a ready-made, cohesive look.

How to Hang a Flower Print Set of 3 in Your Bedroom

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough horizontal space for three prints side by side — above a bed headboard or along an empty feature wall both work brilliantly. Make sure the wall colour complements the soft pinks, greens and whites in the art.

2. Lay them out first: Before putting anything on the wall, lay your three prints on the floor or bed in the order you'd like them. This lets you check the spacing and arrangement without making unnecessary holes.

3. Find your centre point: Mark the centre of your wall lightly with a pencil. Hang the middle print first, centred on this point at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from floor to the centre of the print), then work outwards to the left and right prints with an even gap of around 5–8 cm between each.

4. Use a level: A small spirit level or a level app on your phone keeps all three prints perfectly straight — it takes seconds and makes such a difference to the finished look.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, stand back from across the room to check the overall balance. Small adjustments now save regret later!

Which Flower Print Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print on Luster Paper — A great value choice if you already have frames you love or want to source your own. Luster paper has a gentle sheen that brings out the soft watercolour tones in the flower shop scenes. You choose your own frame and mount.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The premium unframed option. Museum quality paper gives a beautifully crisp, gallery-clean finish that lets every fine detail in the watercolour illustration — every petal, every leaf — really sing. Ideal if you want the sharpest possible print in your own frame.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no frame hunting, no hassle. A brilliant option if you want a polished, finished look quickly. Available in multiple sizes to suit your wall.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed and stretched over a solid frame with the image wrapping around the edges. Gives the art a tactile, painterly quality that suits the cottage watercolour style perfectly. Also arrives ready to hang — no extra framing needed.

What is flower art?

Flower art refers to artwork — prints, paintings or illustrations — where flowers, botanicals or floral scenes are the main subject. It covers everything from loose watercolour studies of individual blooms to detailed botanical illustrations and charming scenes like flower shop facades. Flower art is one of the most popular choices for bedroom walls because it brings colour, softness and a natural, calming feel to a space. It suits a wide range of interior styles, from country cottage and vintage to modern Scandi and maximalist.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Flower Art Prints in Your Bedroom

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough horizontal space to display all three prints side by side — above the bed or along a feature wall both work brilliantly for this set.

2. Decide on your spacing: Lay all three prints out on the floor first to get a feel for the arrangement. A gap of around 5 to 8 cm between each print looks neat and intentional without the pieces feeling disconnected.

3. Find your centre point: Measure the midpoint of your wall and use that as your anchor. Work outwards from the centre so the whole group sits balanced on the wall.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level — around 145 to 150 cm from the floor is a good general rule for a bedroom.

5. Step back and adjust: Once the first print is up, use a spirit level and step back to check everything looks even before committing to the other two hooks. Small adjustments at this stage save a lot of fuss later.

Framed Print — Your chosen print professionally framed and arriving ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra shopping required. Available in multiple sizes with Luster or Museum quality paper.

Paper — Museum Quality — A smooth matte finish with a fine-art feel — ideal if you prefer a quieter, gallery-style look that lets the delicate watercolour detailing speak for itself.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Flower Prints in Your Bedroom
